title: Per-route emergency burst reallocation, billing audit trail, and invoice reconciliation acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Customers can configure per-route quotas and per-account burst pools. We observed a class of operational issues where a single high-traffic route exhausts its route quota and automatically consumes emergency burst credits from the account-level pool, creating negative balances for that route and inconsistent invoice line items. Finance and CS teams need deterministic rules for reallocation, a complete immutable audit trail for every credit movement, and clear invoice adjustments when reallocation or rollback occurs.

Scope: This ticket defines PRD-level acceptance criteria and edge-case handling for: (1) per-route emergency burst reallocation (policy, limits, and TTL), (2) negative-balance reconciliation and automatic vs. manual rollback behavior, (3) immutable billing audit trail and invoice line-item changes, and (4) UI/API surfaces for visibility and dispute. Engineering will implement after acceptance criteria are validated.

Out-of-scope: meter redesign, long-term pricing model changes, multi-tenant credit pooling (separate project), retroactive refunds beyond 90 days (finance policy dependent).
acceptance_criteria: Policy: When a route exceeds its quota and account-level emergency burst pool is enabled, credits will be reallocated automatically up to a per-route emergency limit (configurable; default 5x route quota) and for a time-to-live (TTL) window of 1 hour unless extended by a manual admin action.
Determinism: Reallocation events must be idempotent and produce the same outcome if replayed; sequence numbers and event IDs included in the audit trail to allow exact replay by finance tooling.

Negative-balance reconciliation: If automatic reallocation pushes a route into a negative balance, the system must create a reconciliation job that attempts to settle within 24h by throttling, notifying the customer, and (if settlement fails) marking an invoice adjustment candidate for Finance review.

Invoice changes: Any billing-affecting reallocation or rollback must surface as discrete invoice line items ("Burst Reallocation Credit", "Burst Reclaim Debit") with references to the event ID and timestamps. Invoices generated within 7 days of the event must include the correct delta; older invoices create adjustment rows and a clear note for customers.

Audit trail: All credit movements (automatic and manual) must be recorded immutably with fields: event_id, timestamp, actor (system/user id), from_entity, to_entity, amount_units, reason_code, related_request_id. Audit entries must be available via the Console export (CSV) and a new API endpoint /v1/billing/audit?entity_id=<id>&from=<date>&to=<date> with pagination.

API behavior: Public API responses for routes should include real-time quota state: {remaining, burst_available, pending_reallocations, last_realloc_event_id}. If last_realloc_event_id exists, calling /v1/billing/audit?event_id=<id> returns the canonical audit entry.

UI/Console: Console displays a per-route "Burst History" timeline with events, amounts, and links to invoice line items and the audit export. Design must show a clear remediation button for "Reclaim Burst" with required guardrails (requires Finance role or perms).

Metrics & SLOs: Reallocation pipeline success rate >= 99.5% on 99th percentile of events; audit queries respond < 300ms P95 for 30-day windows. Billing reconciliation accuracy verified by finance smoke tests (sample covering 1000 realloc events) with zero mismatches in amounts.

Dispute flow: If a customer files a billing dispute within 90 days referencing a reallocation, the system must allow Finance to attach the immutable audit export and produce a provisional credit within 5 business days if the audit shows an error. The provisional credit must be flagged and reconciled by the monthly billing close job.

Security & compliance: Audit data for reallocations must be retained per retention policy (default 3 years) and only accessible by roles with billing.audit or billing.read permissions. Any API that returns audit rows must redact PII per privacy policy.
